title: The Compass of Devil's Throat
premise: Astrid Vasquez, a riverboat captain haunted by the family she fled, takes a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to deliver it to his daughter — a promise that drags her into Devil's Throat, a gorge where a rival salvage syndicate, her estranged brother, and the prospector's own buried crimes all converge. As the monsoon traps her leaking boat and forces uneasy alliances with a stranger named Wren, Astrid discovers the map leads not to gold but to the syndicate's ledger of stolen inheritances, including her own family's stolen river rights. In the brief window when glacier calving opens the upper route, Astrid must choose between selling the ledger for freedom or burning it to free everyone it binds; she burns it, claims her name at last, and lets the river take what it will.
about_author: Lena Ishikawa is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on glacial rivers before writing full-time. Her fiction blends nautical grit with quiet moral reckoning, and The Compass of Devil's Throat is her third novel.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She pilots her aging riverboat through shifting channels, establishing her rule: never stop moving, never take passengers who ask questions. A dockside debt collector reminds her why stillness is dangerous. Emotional beat: restless competence masking dread.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Prospector Elias Thorn, coughing blood on her deck, offers a weathered map and a sealed letter if she'll carry them upriver to his daughter before monsoon. She refuses twice, then sees the map bears her father's handwriting. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity tipping into compulsion.

chapters.title: What the River Owes
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present as Astrid accepts the bargain. We learn her family lost their river rights to a syndicate years ago, scattering her kin. She tells herself this is just a delivery job. Emotional beat: grief dressed up as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Passengers with Questions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A stranger boards at Kettle Landing, paying triple fare and asking about Devil's Throat. Wren watches Astrid lie smoothly and wonders which of them is running from more. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpening into wary fascination.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Wake
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A black-hulled syndicate patrol boat shadows them, demanding inspection. Astrid hides the map in the bilge and talks her way past a captain who seems to know her surname. Emotional beat: fear crystallizing into defiance.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, alternating brief POVs. Radio warnings announce early monsoon; the crew debates turning back. Thorn worsens, raving about a ledger hidden 'where the ice keeps time.' Emotional beat: the window closing around them.

chapters.title: Leaking at Mile Forty
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The old hull splits on a submerged log; Wren proves unexpectedly skilled with patchwork repairs, revealing a past in salvage work — possibly syndicate work. Emotional beat: grudging trust built with wet hands and shared labor.

chapters.title: Thorn's Confession
chapters.summary: Thorn's POV, his final night. He reveals he helped the syndicate steal the ledgers of inheritance, including the Vasquez claim, and that the map is his penance. He dies at dawn. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution too late.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They reach the coordinates for Thorn's daughter and find an abandoned homestead and a grave. The letter, opened, names not a daughter but a location inside Devil's Throat itself. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Into the Throat
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, high tension. They enter the gorge's narrow rapids against worsening rain, navigating by memory and instinct while the syndicate boat closes behind. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce focus.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered, Wren confesses: they were sent to recover the map, but reading Thorn's letter changed them — their own family's name appears in the stolen ledgers. Emotional beat: shame becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Brother at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the confluence camp, the syndicate's local chief is revealed to be Astrid's brother Mateo, who sold out years ago and now enforces the thefts he suffered. Emotional beat: love and fury colliding.

chapters.title: Terms of Blood
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. He offers Astrid her family's restored rights in exchange for the map and silence about the ledger. She stalls, seeing how power has hollowed him. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Where the Ice Keeps Time
chapters.summary: Astrid and Wren's alternating POV. Following the map's true bearing, they find a glacier cave holding the syndicate's vault of ledgers — dozens of families' stolen inheritances. Emotional beat: awe and horror at the scale of the theft.

chapters.title: The Long Dark of Monsoon
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Trapped by floodwater at the cave mouth for days, the group fractures: one crew member wants to sell out, another wants revenge. Astrid holds them together with stories and rationed hope. Emotional beat: endurance as intimacy.

chapters.title: What Power Costs
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. Back at the confluence, Mateo's superiors arrive and demand results, threatening him with the same dispossession he administers. He realizes he was never a partner, only a tool. Emotional beat: the corrupter corrupted.

chapters.title: The Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The glacier begins to calve; the route upstream will open for perhaps two days. The syndicate moves to seal the cave. Astrid plans the impossible: run the rapids out with the ledgers aboard a leaking boat. Emotional beat: decisive clarity under pressure.

chapters.title: Running the Throat
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax part one. A desperate daylight run through the gorge as ice groans and the syndicate pursues. Wren takes the wheel during Astrid's injury; Mateo, defecting, blocks the patrol boat with his own vessel. Emotional beat: sacrifice breaking old debts open.

chapters.title: The Burning Ledger
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Astrid's POV. Cornered at the lower landing, Astrid chooses: rather than trade the ledgers for her own restoration, she burns them all — freeing every bound family, including hers, into uncertainty. Emotional beat: liberation through loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The syndicate retreats amid scandal; Mateo, broken but alive, asks nothing and receives a cold nod from his sister. Wren chooses to stay with Astrid, no longer a stranger. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Name on the Boat
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She repaints the boat's faded nameplate with her full name — Vasquez — for the first time in a decade, claiming the inheritance that can't be stolen: her history. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed quietly.

chapters.title: Compass Points
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. Monsoon ends; the river settles into new channels, sandbars rearranged. Astrid and Wren take on honest cargo, and when a young traveler asks about Devil's Throat, Astrid says only, 'It costs less than stopping used to.' Emotional beat: peace earned, motion chosen freely.
